7.0.0.en: Our Lord Jesus Christ warns us not to judge others, that is, to be distressed by their faults, forgetting that we are sinners like them, and deserve that God should judge us. But by humility we receive God's forgiveness. For when we find excuses for others and show them mercy, God also has mercy on us and forgives us our sins.

7.0.1.en: So judging is not only a lack of repentance and a lack of love for others, but an encroachment on the authority of God the Judge, for we take His place and judge others.

7.0.2.en: It also carries pride in the heart, and contempt for the sinner. And not judging does not mean not discerning; rather we must discern the sin, and pray for the sinner, and love him, and find an excuse for him, and have compassion on him as a father, but we keep away from his sin and rebuke it as far as we are able, so we separate between the sin and the sinner, that is, we hate the sin and love the sinner.

7.0.3.en: "Measure": it is a vessel for measuring the volume of grain, and what is meant here is the vessel that we fill with judgment and pour out upon others, which is poured out upon us also with the same vessel, as judgment from God, and in many cases He permits us to fall into the same sin for which we judge others, until we repent and are humbled.

7.1.0.en: "Mote": a small straw or chaff, and it signifies a small sin.

7.1.1.en: "Beam": a piece of wood much larger than the mote, which blocks the sight, and signifies a great sin. Christ likens the sin of the other to the mote in his eye, but my sin to a beam in my eye, so repentance is first necessary to remove the beam from my eye, so my life is purified, and consequently I am able, by love and the work of the Holy Spirit, to see the mote that is in the other's eye, that is, his sin, and help him to be rid of it.

7.1.2.en: But my neglecting the beam in my eye by not repenting, and then presuming to judge others, pretending in hypocrisy that I want to help them remove the mote, which is a very small straw, from their eyes, is unreasonable, for how can the one whose eyes the beam blocks see a small mote in the eyes of others?!

7.1.3.en: The truth is that it is pride that drives us to judge others and not repent of our sins.

7.1.4.en: In conclusion, care for your repentance every day and pray for others if they err, and find an excuse for them.

7.2.0.en: The meaning of simplicity and love in dealing with others, so that we do not judge them, is not that we speak about the holy sacraments in the Church and the works of the Holy Spirit before unbelievers who do not appreciate their importance. In ancient times the Church used to close the doors after the catechumens were sent out, so that only the faithful remained who would partake of the Mysteries.

7.2.1.en: "Dogs": they signify attack, so they represent those who resist the truth.

7.2.2.en: "Swine": in their lack of understanding, they trample and defile everything because of their filthiness, so they signify contempt for the truth.

7.2.3.en: That is, simplicity is joined with wisdom in dealing with others.

7.2.4.en: Among holy things also are personal spiritual experiences, which are not told except to the father of confession, or without mentioning the name, so that we keep our humility, and do not expose these divine dealings to the lack of appreciation of others. You need to discern between truth and falsehood, and between the righteous and the wicked, but you say the suitable word at the suitable time, so do not speak to beginners about high spiritual matters that make life with God difficult. You have the right to ask and understand everything for the growth of your spiritual life, but speak only of what benefits you and benefits others.

7.3.0.en: God, in His fatherly love, wants to give us everything. But He gives only to the one who appreciates the gift, and this appreciation appears in asking for it from God.

7.3.1.en: God gives general gifts to all mankind, such as the sun, the air, the water ... and so on. But, in His love, He wants to give more than this. So if He finds us neglectful of praying to Him, He stirs us to ask Him, so that we receive from Him ... and if He delays in answering to test our faith, we ask from Him and press Him, and so find our needs in Him. And if God's door remains closed and He does not answer, we knock until He opens to us, and we are confident that He will surely answer all who pray to Him, as long as their prayers are according to His will and for their good.

7.4.0.en: Christ offers us a logical proof of His fatherly love. Human fatherhood cares for the requests of the children, and cannot give them the opposite of their requests, as long as the need is real, necessary and beneficial. No father gives his son a stone instead of bread, or a serpent instead of fish, to eat.

7.4.1.en: If fatherhood according to the flesh has this love, how much more God, the source of fatherhood and love, who gives good things to His children who trust Him and ask their needs from Him?!

7.4.2.en: "Evil": all mankind, because they fall into evil, but by instinct they care to give good gifts to their children. "Your Father which is in heaven": showing that God is the source of fatherhood and tenderness.

7.4.3.en: "Good things": that is, good gifts that His children need.

7.4.4.en: "To them that ask him": those who hold fast to their prayers in faith and persistence, and rely on God.

7.4.5.en: Do not listen to the devil's doubts if God delays in answering your requests, but press Him, confident of His love, and that He gives you at the suitable time what is for your good.

7.5.0.en: In order that God may answer our requests, we must do good to others. If we want them to do good to us, let us begin first to do so; for love of others is the fulfillment of the commandment and the Law. When you meet any person, put yourself in his place, and think what he expects from you, so that you offer him the love he needs, or the care and sympathy and support he awaits. And if someone wrongs you, do not hasten to answer him or judge him in your heart, but feel his circumstances so as to find an excuse for him and be tender toward him, even if only with a prayer in your heart.

7.6.0.en: "False prophets": they are those who teach doctrines foreign to the Church, and deceive people with their pleasant appearance, but their hearts within are savage and harsh. They think inwardly of what is for their own benefit, and not for the glory of God as they claim; so Christ warns us to keep away from them and to remain steadfast in the Church. "Sheep's clothing": that is, they are wolves with the appearance of lambs, meaning their pretending to piety and virtues in order to deceive the simple, and draw them away from the Church and its gatherings, and make them attach themselves to foreign gatherings, and deceive them that this is the right interpretation of the word of God.

7.7.0.en: To know the truth about these prophets, we look at their "fruits", that is, their character and deeds, because if the heart is harsh, however much it pretends, its harshness will be exposed in some situations.

7.7.1.en: "Thorns": they represent the absence of blessing and the wronging of others, so they make no sacrifice (which is signified by the grape that is pressed and yields wine, that is, joy), for the selfish, harsh person does not care to give of himself for others. "Thistles": a dry plant resembling thorns in its smallness, which cannot give figs.

7.7.2.en: The fig fruit: it is made of small seeds united together in love inside a single covering, so it signifies unity and love.

7.7.3.en: The person who is isolated in selfishness alone cannot be united with others in a oneness of love. So it is natural that the good tree, that is, the heart that loves God, will give good fruits. And the opposite is true, for the evil person will do evils.

7.7.4.en: So the heart must be changed by repentance, that the fruits may become good.

7.8.0.en: "Is cast into the fire": just as it is customary to burn useless trees, so these false teachers have nothing awaiting them but torment in the eternal fire.

7.8.1.en: If these wicked persist in their misleading teachings, their end will be perdition, that is, the eternal fire. So we must be careful before following any person, and be certain of his conduct and virtues, and that he is a son of the Church and submissive to the spiritual fathers.

7.8.2.en: Be discerning toward those around you while keeping your love for them. Do not be led after teachings foreign to the spirit of the Church, or attend gatherings that do not have the official character and church affiliation, or host people you do not know on the pretext that they will speak to you about God. Remain steadfast in your Church and your holy sacraments and your spiritual gatherings, and so you grow in the knowledge and love of God.

7.9.0.en: Christ concludes His Sermon on the Mount by affirming the importance of acting on His commandments, and not merely hearing them and admiring them.

7.9.1.en: "Wise": that is, he examines his life and is careful in his conduct.

7.9.2.en: The one who acts on the commandment He likens to a man who wanted to build a house to live in, so he dug in the ground and deepened the digging until he reached the rock, and laid the foundation of his house on it, then built it and raised it into the air; and when the sky rained violent torrents, and the torrents rushed like rivers and struck this house, accompanied by stormy winds, they could not shake it, because it was founded on the rock.

7.9.3.en: "The rock": it points to Christ, since He said of Himself that He is the chief cornerstone (ch. 21:42), and the Apostle Paul said that Christ is the foundation on which the spiritual house is built (1 Cor 3:11), so the foundation must be laid on Him, that is, faith in Him, for building our spiritual life, steadfast in the Church, His body, and united with Him in the holy sacraments.

7.9.4.en: "The rain ... the floods": they signify material desires.

7.9.5.en: "The winds": they signify temptations and the wars of Satan.

7.9.6.en: If these rise against us, they will not be able to shake our life, because we obey the commandments of Christ.

7.10.0.en: "Foolish": he does not want to understand or to labor in caring for the salvation of his soul. The one who is content with knowing Christ, and does not want to labor in carrying out His commandments, is like one who does not want the labor of deep digging, that is, he refuses to carry the cross, and to go deeper in the knowledge of God and the carrying out of His commandments, since he is a lover of appearances.

7.10.1.en: "Sand": it signifies weakness of faith, and likewise the false speech of heresies, which promises people salvation without striving.

7.10.2.en: Since they refuse the labor of carrying out the commandment, if temptations and the devil's wars rise against them, their whole spiritual building falls, and they go far from God, and their end is eternal perdition.

7.10.3.en: "Great": that is, a complete collapse of the person, and eternal perdition.

7.10.4.en: Commit yourself to a specific spiritual discipline every day, so that the word of God which you read may be turned into practical action in your life.

8.0.0.en: Since the crowds were moved by His words, hearts were attached to Him, so they followed Him to hear more of His sermons.

8.0.1.en: And Christ welcomed them so as to work His miracles before them, and so establish their faith. And He walked on the plain beside the Sea of Tiberias on His way to the city of Capernaum.

8.1.0.en: The disease of leprosy appears in the form of spots on the skin, so it resembles the present disease of vitiligo, and also some of the affected parts can separate from the body, so it also resembles the disease of leprosy (Hansen's disease), and it signifies uncleanness, and whoever is struck by it must be isolated from people whatever his position, and must tear his clothes and cover his moustache and bare his head. And if someone approaches him, he cries: "Unclean, unclean", to warn him to keep away from him (Lev 13:45). This disease no longer exists at present.

8.1.1.en: And while Christ was coming down from the mountain (and this signifies Christ's condescension in love to heal our uncleanness and weakness), He cleansed this Jewish leper (an indication of the cleansing of the Jewish nation from foreign teachings) and its return to the commandments of God.

8.1.2.en: This leper met Christ outside the city, where he was isolated, because he had heard of His teachings and His power in healing diseases.

8.1.3.en: "Worshipped him": a declaration of his faith in Christ and his humility before Him.

8.1.4.en: "If thou wilt": a polite form in addressing Christ, and a surrender to His will.

8.1.5.en: "Thou canst": confidence and faith in Christ the Healer.

8.1.6.en: Believe in God's power to forgive your sin, and ask His help, and He frees you from it, and gives you the feelings of repentance and confession, however great your weakness.

8.2.0.en: Christ commanded the leper to be cleansed, and joined His word with action, and touched him, and he was healed immediately, and the color of his skin changed and returned to normal.

8.2.1.en: Christ touched him to teach us to join our words with deeds, and to declare His authority and His purity, which is not affected by touching the unclean, but cleanses them, because He is God, who is able to cleanse.

8.2.2.en: And so too, if we live in purity of heart, we are not defiled by evil if circumstances compel us to face it in the world.

8.3.0.en: "Tell no man": because Christ does not seek honor from people, and because His aim in the miracles is to establish His teachings and not to dazzle the crowds.

8.3.1.en: And Christ declared that He does not break the Law but fulfills it by sending the leper whom He healed to offer a sacrifice according to the Law, after the priest examines him and makes sure of his healing, and so that this might be a proclamation to the Jewish priests to believe in Him, when they see that His authority is stronger than theirs in the power to heal.

8.3.2.en: "The gift": which the Law commanded, which is two birds (Lev 14:4).

8.4.s.en: (2) The healing of the centurion's servant

8.4.0.en: "Came": it appears from (Lk 7:3) that he sent elders of the Jews to Christ, to ask in his name for the healing of his servant, and the coming is attributed here to the centurion because the elders were delegates for him.

8.4.1.en: "A centurion": in charge of a Roman unit of a hundred soldiers, found in large cities such as Capernaum. He was a pagan man, but devout and loving the Jews.

8.4.2.en: Jesus then entered the city of Capernaum, a large city in Galilee, and a centurion came to Him and asked Him to heal one of his servants who was afflicted with paralysis and lay at home; and this shows the tenderness of this centurion and his care for his servants.

8.4.3.en: "Grievously tormented": some kinds of paralysis are accompanied by severe pains, or he may have been tormented in spirit by being laid on his bed and unable to move and do what he needs.

8.4.4.en: This signifies the Gentiles' turning to Christ, to save them from the spiritual paralysis into which they fell by their worship of idols, and their souls were tormented by it.

8.5.0.en: Jesus showed His love for the Gentiles as for the Jews, and His readiness to enter their houses and heal them, for He does not despise the Gentiles; and in humility, He is ready to go to them, because He became incarnate for the salvation of the whole world. "I will come and heal him": this declares His complete power to heal.

8.6.0.en: "I am not worthy": despite the position of this centurion, and the Romans' habit of despising the Jews, this centurion showed unexpected humility before Christ.

8.6.1.en: "Under my roof": because the Jews do not enter the houses of the Gentiles, Christ would not be embarrassed if he invited Him to heal his servant. The centurion said humbly to Christ that he was not worthy that He should visit him in his house to heal his servant, and declared his faith that one word from Christ is able to heal. For he is a commander and has authority over his soldiers, so how much more Christ, the great God, has authority over everything.

8.6.2.en: "Under authority": that is, under the authority of commanders in the army greater than I, or under the authority of the king, yet I am able to command my servant and he obeys me, so how much more You, who are able to do all things?!

8.7.0.en: Christ marveled at this faith and praised it, declaring that it was greater than any faith that appeared among the Jews. For God is just and gives every person his due honor.

8.8.0.en: "From the east and west": that is, from the Gentiles, and this is a clear declaration from Christ that His Kingdom includes the Gentiles also like the Jews.

8.8.1.en: He added that many of the Gentiles will believe and precede into the Kingdom where Abraham and the Fathers are, and at the same time many of the Jews, whom He calls "the children of the kingdom", since God chose them as His special people, and gave them His commandments, and was born among them to save them, will refuse to believe, and so will be cast into eternal torment outside the Kingdom, which He expresses as "darkness" where the light of Christ is not found.

8.8.2.en: "Gnashing of teeth": it represents torment, anger and despair.

8.9.0.en: Christ granted healing by His word from a distance, and the servant was healed immediately, and the centurion enjoyed joy because of his faith, and this shows two important things:

8.9.2.en: (2) The importance of intercession in God's sight, by Christ's answering the centurion's request for his servant. If someone asks you for a service, have compassion on him and hasten to help him, indeed may you have compassion on the weary around you before they ask you, and be ready to spend all effort to help them, giving up your dignity for their comfort, confident that this is the greatest thing in God's sight, that is, the work of mercy.

8.10.0.en: "Peter's house": he had a house in Capernaum, although he was originally from Bethsaida.

8.10.1.en: "His wife's mother": this means that he was married, and his marriage did not hinder him from following Christ and serving Him. "Laid, and sick of a fever": it appears from this that the fever was severe and deprived her of the ability to move and work.

8.10.2.en: "He touched her hand": to proclaim to the people in a tangible way His power to heal, and that He is the source of the health that the sick woman would receive.

8.10.3.en: And Christ here cares for His servants; if they have followed Him and relied on Him, He cares for all their affairs, and heals their diseases and those of their families; Christ takes special care of His children who serve.

8.10.4.en: In this miracle there is also concern for women and a welcome of their service, since when He healed her, she arose and ministered to them. And from the spiritual side, the fever signifies the spiritual diseases that hinder the soul from its life with God and its service of Him. But when we take refuge in Him, He heals us and we regain our first strength.

8.11.0.en: The news of Christ's miracles spread throughout Capernaum. And because the day was a Sabbath, as our teacher Mark the Apostle mentions (Mk 1:21), they brought the sick to Him in the evening, that is, after the end of the Sabbath day on which they do no work (Mk 1:32). They were sick with various bodily diseases, or demons dwelt in them and caused them diseases such as madness, and He healed them all by His love and tenderness. For He came to take away our diseases, and He bore all our sufferings on the Cross and redeemed us, as Isaiah prophesied (Isa 53:4). God seeks the weary, and goes to them to heal them, as He became incarnate to take away our troubles. Therefore let us be encouraged and take refuge in Him in all our needs, confident of His fatherhood and love, and also His power to solve all our problems. Let us not rely on our minds and abilities or the abilities of those around us, for all are of no use unless they are in God's hand; and in this our heart is always assured of His being with us, and we do not worry about anything that may happen in the future.

8.12.0.en: The great crowds followed Christ to enjoy His sermons and see His miracles, so He told His disciples who were close to Him to cross from the western shore of the Sea of Galilee to the eastern shore, which is about six miles, that is, it takes about two hours by ship, so that there might be an opportunity to preach in other places, and also as rest for His body and His disciples, and so as to escape from the Jews who wanted to set Him up as an earthly king who would free them from the Romans, because His Kingdom is greater than this, being the Kingdom of Heaven.

8.13.0.en: As He was going to the shore, one of the scribes came to Him, who are an advanced group among the Jews, knowing the holy Scriptures, because they were concerned with copying them, and consequently knowing what is in them. This scribe asked to be a follower of Christ in every place, after seeing His authority over diseases, so that he might have a position in the new kingdom which the Jews thought He would set up on earth.

8.14.0.en: Christ's reply to him was that He was poor, having no dwelling to live in like the rest of mankind, or even the animals such as the foxes which have dwellings, that is, holes called dens, nor like the birds which have dwellings that are their nests, that is, their roosts, but He used to spend the night in any place where they hosted Him, or sometimes slept in the boat, and at other times spent the whole night praying in secret.

8.14.1.en: And Christ's reply shows that this scribe's aim was to obtain a material position, and not love and seeking discipleship to Him.

8.14.2.en: Ask yourself in your following of Christ: is it for love of Him or to obtain material requests? And do you grumble if God does not answer your prayer, or delays in answering?

8.14.3.en: Try to understand God's purposes, because His aim in all His dealings with you is the salvation of your soul and your drawing near to Him, even if this requires you to pass through some tribulations, or to lack some material things.

8.15.0.en: Another person came forward from the followers of Christ and those who were being discipled at His hands, but not one of the twelve disciples, declaring his readiness to continue following Him without any material purpose, unlike the scribe who asked to follow Christ in the previous verse, but he asked Christ's leave to bury his father. What is meant is not merely the burial of the body, but the ceremonies of burial and condolence which took a long time, and procedures for dividing the inheritance might be connected with them, and they also attach the heart emotionally to many griefs that could occupy it from the salvation of its soul.

8.16.0.en: Christ said to him that he must concentrate on following Him, and not be occupied with the customs of people and their many worldly concerns.

8.16.1.en: "The dead": he means those alive in body but dead in spirit, that is, who do not believe in Christ and do not care for the salvation of their souls. These are the relatives and friends of the dead man who will be occupied with the ceremonies of burial and condolence. This disciple's attachment to passing material things would hinder him from God, so let him leave the spiritually dead to be occupied with material things, but let him be free for God.

8.16.2.en: It is understood from this that Christ does not mean merely the burial of the body of the dead, but not being hindered from following Him by any excessive emotional attachments, and not ordinary emotion in the burial of the dead, or love of those around us; on the contrary, we carry out our duties toward our parents and all our loved ones for God's sake, and our goal is clear before us, which is the salvation of our souls.

8.17.0.en: Christ entered the ship to cross the Sea of Tiberias, that is, the Sea of Galilee, to the eastern side, and slept inside the ship.

8.17.1.en: "A great tempest": the Sea of Tiberias was far below sea level, and surrounded by mountains, and consequently exposed to sudden winds that stir up its waves.

8.17.2.en: "Asleep": besides the fact that Christ's sleeping confirms His humanity, and His need for sleep and rest, it was a deliberate sleep so as to test the faith of His disciples, and from another side, their helplessness appears, despite their experience in fishing and sailing the sea, so that they feel the need for God the Savior.

8.17.3.en: The ship faced violent winds, and the waves rose until they covered it, and it was about to sink.

8.17.4.en: The winds signify temptations, and the waves the troubled world, and the ship our life in which Christ dwells, but He is asleep, that is, not working in us, because of our not taking refuge in Him, and our reliance on our own strength, whose helplessness appears before the cruelty of the devil's wars.

8.18.0.en: At last, when the disciples were certain of their helplessness, they took refuge in Christ, declaring that they were perishing, because of their weakness before the violence of the winds and waves, asking Him to save them.

8.19.0.en: Before Christ showed His authority over nature, He rebuked their little faith. For after they had seen His miracles, they should have trusted and believed in His divinity, and not feared the waves; then He commanded the winds and the waves and they grew calm. "O ye of little faith": they have faith and therefore they took refuge in Him, but it is little, as is proved by their fear and lack of trust in His complete power to save them.

8.19.1.en: "Rebuked": a declaration of the divinity of Christ and His authority over nature, as though He were commanding a person and he obeyed Him. "A great calm": it shows the power of the miracle in the stilling of the winds and waves at once and completely.

8.19.2.en: If a temptation meets you or you fall into sin, hasten to awaken the Christ who sleeps in you with a prayer of supplication and humility, and He will save you and restore your peace to you.

8.20.0.en: Before Christ's authority over nature, and the appearance of the power of His divinity, the disciples marveled, and their faith began to grow, and their knowledge of Christ the true God increased.

8.21.s.en: (6) The two madmen in the country of the Gergesenes

8.21.0.en: "Unto the other side": Christ reached by ship the eastern shore of the Sea of Galilee.

8.21.1.en: "The country of the Gergesenes": a village situated among the lands of the Gadarenes, on the eastern shore of the Sea of Tiberias. Two madmen who lived in the tombs of this city ran quickly toward Christ. It seems that one of them was more violent than the other, so our teachers Mark and Luke mentioned him (Mk 5:1-20; Lk 8:26-39), and omitted mentioning the second madman. Because of their great violence, they blocked the way for passers-by, so people feared to pass along this road.

8.21.2.en: And the demons dwelt in these two madmen and deprived them of their minds, and they no longer enjoyed the natural peace that belongs to human beings.

8.21.3.en: This is the action of the cruel demons upon careless human beings, when they go far from God. Indeed more than this, they, by their violence, prevented others from passing along this road, for Satan tries to hinder people from passing along the way of God.

8.22.0.en: The demons could not bear to see Christ, and cried out in weakness and fear of His authority not to torment them. A large group of demons dwelt in these two madmen, and not one demon, therefore they spoke in the plural.

8.22.1.en: "Before the time": that is, before the day of judgment.

8.22.2.en: "To torment us": to destroy us and cast us into eternal torment.

8.23.0.en: Near the city were hills on which herds of swine were feeding, numbering about two thousand (Mk 5:13), and the demons asked Christ, if He wished to cast them out of the two madmen, to permit them to enter the swine. This shows clearly Christ's authority over the demons, for they do not move without His permission, and it also shows the wickedness of the demons, who wish to kill the swine to stir up their owners against Christ and prevent His preaching.

8.24.0.en: Christ permitted them to enter the swine, and they rushed from the shore into the sea and all were drowned.

8.24.1.en: This shows the cruelty of the demons who want to destroy us, but Christ did not permit them to destroy the two madmen, and permitted only the destruction of the swine, because swine are forbidden among the Jews, so raising them was against the divine Law. And this shows that the violence and madness in the two madmen was not a nervous disease, but the work of the demons. "A steep place": that is, from the foot of the mountain to the edge of the sea.

8.25.0.en: The herdsmen were greatly disturbed by the power of the miracle, and grieved over the loss of their wealth, and told the Gergesenes, the inhabitants of the city, who went out and saw Christ, and feared His power, and grieved over the loss of the city's possessions, which were these swine. And in hardness of heart, they did not care about the healing of the two madmen, because their attachment to material things blinded their eyes, and they did not see the divine grace with which they could have been blessed by Christ, but feared losing something else material, so they asked Christ not to enter their city.

8.25.1.en: Christ left them because of their attachment to material things, although at the same time He sent the two healed madmen to preach in His name "in Decapolis" (Mk 5:20), which are the cities surrounding their city.

8.25.2.en: The love of money and material things blinds your eyes to understanding the works of God, and even makes you reject the work of His grace in you, so you lose Christ's dwelling in your heart. Therefore try to feel for those around you and strive to serve them, and sacrifice some of the material things you have, so that you become alert and your eyes are opened, and you see the work of God offered to you.

8.25.3.en: The healing of the sick; the casting out of demons; the raising of Jairus's daughter
